es.summary: Una identidad creó, modificó o eliminó un Job o CronJob de Kubernetes (API group batch). Puede ser un cambio legítimo o un intento de ejecutar código o lograr persistencia en el clúster.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos del audit log de Kubernetes con objectRef.apiGroup igual a batch, objectRef.resource igual a jobs o cronjobs y verb igual a create, delete, patch, replace o update.
es.why_it_matters: Un atacante con permisos sobre batch puede programar un CronJob que lance contenedores maliciosos de forma recurrente (persistencia y ejecución, ATT&CK T1053.007, Container Orchestration Job). Si el pod usa una service account privilegiada o hostPath, permite escalar privilegios. Eliminar Jobs puede ocultar rastros.
triage_steps: Identifique quién actuó: user.username, user.groups, sourceIPs y userAgent. Distinga kubectl manual, pipelines de CI/CD y controladores del sistema.
Revise objectRef.namespace, objectRef.name, verb y responseStatus.code; un intento rechazado (403) también indica reconocimiento o abuso de credenciales.
Si el usuario es system:serviceaccount:kube-system:cronjob-controller creando jobs, valide que el CronJob padre sea conocido y descarte el evento si lo es.
Obtenga el manifiesto (requestObject o kubectl get -o yaml): imagen, registro, command/args, schedule, serviceAccountName, privileged, hostPath, hostNetwork.
Busque imágenes de registros no confiables, comandos con curl, wget, base64, shells inversas o mineros, y schedules muy frecuentes.
Pivotee sobre el mismo usuario y sourceIPs en +/- 15 minutos: creación de RoleBindings, secrets leídos, exec en pods u otros cambios en kube-system.
Compare con tickets de cambio, commits de GitOps (Argo CD, Flux) y alertas previas para la misma identidad o namespace.
false_positives: Administradores que crean o ajustan Jobs y CronJobs de mantenimiento, backups o migraciones.
Pipelines de CI/CD, Helm u operadores GitOps que despliegan o actualizan workloads batch.
El cronjob-controller creando Jobs a partir de CronJobs existentes y el TTL controller eliminando Jobs terminados.
Operadores de terceros que gestionan Jobs (por ejemplo, de bases de datos o certificados).
response_steps: Confirme con el responsable del namespace o del pipeline si el cambio estaba autorizado.
Si no lo estaba, suspenda el CronJob (spec.suspend=true) y conserve el manifiesto y los logs de los pods antes de eliminar nada.
Revoque o rote las credenciales, tokens o kubeconfig de la identidad usada y revise sus RBAC.
Investigue los nodos donde corrieron los pods y elimine los objetos maliciosos tras documentarlos.
Restrinja permisos sobre batch, aplique políticas de admisión para registros confiables y Pod Security Standards.
es.severity_rationale: Medium es adecuado porque los cambios en Jobs y CronJobs son frecuentes y legítimos, pero un uso malicioso otorga ejecución persistente en el clúster.

en.summary: An identity created, modified or deleted a Kubernetes Job or CronJob (batch API group). This may be a routine change or an attempt to run code or persist in the cluster.
en.what_it_detects: Kubernetes audit events where objectRef.apiGroup is batch, objectRef.resource is jobs or cronjobs, and verb is create, delete, patch, replace or update.
en.why_it_matters: An attacker with batch permissions can schedule a CronJob that repeatedly launches malicious containers (persistence and execution, ATT&CK T1053.007 Container Orchestration Job). Privileged service accounts or hostPath mounts enable privilege escalation; deleting Jobs can hide traces.
triage_steps: Identify the actor: user.username, user.groups, sourceIPs and userAgent. Separate manual kubectl, CI/CD pipelines and system controllers.
Check objectRef.namespace, objectRef.name, verb and responseStatus.code; denied attempts (403) still suggest reconnaissance or credential misuse.
If the user is system:serviceaccount:kube-system:cronjob-controller creating jobs, confirm the parent CronJob is known and close if so.
Retrieve the manifest (requestObject or kubectl get -o yaml): image, registry, command/args, schedule, serviceAccountName, privileged, hostPath, hostNetwork.
Look for untrusted registries, commands using curl, wget, base64, reverse shells or miners, and unusually frequent schedules.
Pivot on the same user and sourceIPs within +/- 15 minutes: RoleBinding creation, secret reads, pod exec or other kube-system changes.
Compare with change tickets, GitOps commits (Argo CD, Flux) and earlier alerts for the same identity or namespace.
false_positives: Administrators creating or adjusting maintenance, backup or migration Jobs and CronJobs.
CI/CD pipelines, Helm or GitOps operators deploying or updating batch workloads.
The cronjob-controller spawning Jobs from existing CronJobs and the TTL controller deleting finished Jobs.
Third-party operators that manage Jobs (for example database or certificate operators).
response_steps: Confirm with the namespace or pipeline owner whether the change was authorized.
If not, suspend the CronJob (spec.suspend=true) and preserve the manifest and pod logs before deleting anything.
Revoke or rotate the credentials, tokens or kubeconfig used and review that identity's RBAC.
Investigate nodes where the pods ran and remove malicious objects after documenting them.
Restrict batch permissions, enforce admission policies for trusted registries and apply Pod Security Standards.
en.severity_rationale: Medium fits because Job and CronJob changes are common and usually legitimate, yet malicious use grants persistent code execution in the cluster.
